answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a bond before trading and by assigning it limited influence until it earns reputation. Random audits sample coordinated accounts; when linked fake identities are exposed, their bonds are slashed and their recent rewards voided. The attacker therefore pays capital for every alias, risks losing it on detection, and must repeat the expense to rebuild trust, making an atlas of fakes costly to spread across a canyon or up a knoll.
